files_reviewed: backend/api/views/apply.py (1-60, 370-966, admin-only routes 60-370 by route list only)
frontend/src/components (grep across all files for storage, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, eval, keys, URLs, setTimeout, TODO, console.log, success toasts, sample data)
note: No committed .env or secret values found in code, workflows or tests (.env files are gitignored and not in the repo). Database is MongoDB through MongoEngine, so row level security does not apply and database_rules has no labels. The only model call is server-side OpenAI message moderation, and flagged messages go to an admin review queue, so ai_browser_call and ai_no_human_review have no labels. The biggest gaps are auth: /auth/register lets anyone mint a support-role token that passes admin_only, several profile routes return or mint tokens for existing Firebase users with no password, many routes have their login decorator commented out, and socket messages are broadcast to every connected client. Large admin-only views (admin_dashboard, admin_onboarding, admin_oauth, download) and large frontend admin components were covered by route lists, greps and targeted reads, not line by line. Test files were only grepped for secrets.

labels.what: POST /auth/register mints a Firebase custom token with the role the client sends. Only role 0 (admin) is checked against a whitelist. Role 5 (support) passes admin_only, so anyone can register as staff

POST /auth/newRegister has no login, takes the role from the client and puts it in a custom token. The error check is commented out at lines 155-156, and it passes the plain password to PartnerProfile, which has no password field, so the route crashes after creating the Firebase user
SUPPORT role passes every role check, including admin_only, mentor_only and mentee_only. Support staff can delete accounts and reset any user's email and password

GET /api/accounts/<type> has no login (decorator commented out). Anonymous callers get full admin, support, moderator, guest and partner records. Mentor records include email and phone. With ?all=true it returns private mentee profiles too
GET /api/accounts/<type>/search has no login. It searches mentors and mentees by email, and show_private=true or all=true returns private mentee profiles

GET /api/account/<id> has no login (decorator commented out). For a partner id it returns every assigned mentee's and mentor's direct messages and the hub invite_key. For a mentee or mentor id it returns the full profile including phone number

POST /api/account is public. If the email already exists in Firebase it reuses that uid with no password check, then returns a custom token for it at line 1215. A stranger can get a token tied to another user's Firebase account. It also never checks that the application was approved
POST /api/accountProfile has no login. It looks up any existing Firebase user by email and returns a custom token for that uid with a client-chosen role

PUT /api/account/<id> has no ownership check. Any user with the same role, and any hub, can edit another profile. edit_profile copies the email from the body for mentors, mentees and partners, and the new email is pushed to Firebase at line 1460, so the attacker can then reset the password. A hub can also change another hub's invite_key
PUT /api/account/<id>/image skips all checks when no Authorization header is sent, so anyone can replace any mentor, mentee or partner photo

Public bug-report endpoint with no login or rate limit. It uploads up to 3 attachments of any type to public cloud storage and emails staff an HTML body built from unescaped user input (description, name, page_url)
Bug report recipients hardcoded to two staff email addresses

Rate limit on /api/error/report keys on the client-sent X-Forwarded-For header in an in-memory dict, so changing the header bypasses it. Each report can email developers. The limit of 20 per minute is hardcoded
GET /api/admin/<id> has no login and returns the admin record with email and Firebase uid
Comment holds a real-looking admin record with a personal email and Firebase uid
Upload of allowed emails stores the admin-supplied password in plain text on every VerifiedEmail row
GET /api/notifications/unread_alert_group/<id> has no login. Anyone can make the platform email any partner or hub, with a link and title taken from the query string
GET /api/notifications/unread_alert/<id> has no login (decorator commented out) and sends email and SMS to the user
GET /api/notifications/weeklyemails has no login (decorator commented out because of JWT problems). One request emails every mentee and mentor with unread messages
PUT /api/notifications/update marks messages read for any sender and recipient pair. The ids come from the body and are not tied to the caller
Unread message count for any user id, not tied to the caller
GET /api/meeting/generateToken has no login and signs an 8x8 JaaS meeting token for anyone
Every meeting token carries placeholder identity: 'User Name', 'email_address@email.com' and avatar 'https://asda.com/avatar'
GET /api/translation/ has no login. It loops over every mentor, mentee and partner and saves each one
Any logged-in user of any role can overwrite any mentor's availability
Any mentee can change another mentee's favorite mentors because mentee_id comes from the body
Any mentee can read another mentee's favorites by id
GET /api/training/getSignedDocfile/<id>/<role> has no login and returns any signed PDF
GET /api/training/getSignedDoc/<role> has no login and lists all signed document records with user emails
PATCH /api/training/update_multiple has no login and changes the sort order of any training
DELETE /api/training/library/<id> has no login and deletes any community library item
PUT /api/training/library/<id> has no login and renames or replaces the file of any community library item
POST /api/training/saveSignedDoc has no login. Anyone can upload or overwrite the signed PDF for any user email and training
POST /api/training/new_library has no login. It creates library items with any file and client-chosen user_id, hub_id and user_name
Unauthenticated routes call the paid Google translation API twice per request with no rate limit (also lines 450 and 453 in the library edit route)
Public training list takes a user_email query param and reveals which trainings that email has signed. It also attaches hub emails to each training

POST announcement/register/<role> checks hub ownership only when hub_id is sent. Any logged-in user can post a general announcement to all mentors, mentees or partners and email them all, with a client-supplied front_url as the link base
PUT announcement/upload/<id>/image has no login and replaces any announcement image
GET announcement/getDoc/<id> has no login and returns the attached file, including hub-scoped announcements
GET announcement/get/<id> is public by design but also returns hub-scoped announcements that the list route restricts
GET /api/application/email/status/<email>/<role> has no login and tells anyone whether an email is in Firebase, verified and has a profile
GET /api/application/status/<email>/<role> has no login and returns the full application record for any email, including phone, immigrant status and identity answers
GET /api/application/profile/exists/<email>/<role> has no login and reveals which role an email holds
POST /api/application/changeStateTraining has no login and sets the training status on any application by id

GET /api/application/changeStateBuildProfile/<email>/<role> has no login. It moves any approved application forward and emails the applicant and every admin, with the link base taken from the query string
Public application form has no rate limit or captcha. Each submission emails the applicant and every admin
Any logged-in user can read any mentor's or mentee's appointment requests by id. The GET also writes mentee_id on matching records
Any logged-in user can email any mentee an invite in the name of any mentor. Both ids come from the body
Create appointment takes mentor_id, mentee_id and status from the body with no link to the caller. It emails both people and texts the mentor
Any mentor can accept any appointment. There is no check that the appointment is theirs
Any mentor can deny any appointment. There is no check that the appointment is theirs
Production URL app.menteeglobal.org hardcoded in the SMS text
GET /api/messages/ passes raw query args into Message.objects.filter, so any logged-in user can query any Message by any field or operator
Any logged-in user can delete any Message by id
Any logged-in user can set any field on any Message by id (mass assignment)
Contact mentor takes mentee_id from the body, so any logged-in user can message and email a mentor as any mentee
Any logged-in user can soft-delete any group message
When hub_user_id is omitted, any logged-in user reads all partner group messages
Socket handler editGroupMessage has no sender or ownership check. Any connected user can edit any hub or partner group message
Socket handler sendGroup trusts sender_id and hub_user_id from the client. Any connected user can post into any hub group as anyone
Socket handler invite has no check. Any connected user can send invite events as anyone and add mentors to any mentee's favorites

socketio.emit uses the recipient id as the event name with no room, so each direct message is broadcast to every connected socket. Any logged-in client can listen on another user's id. Same pattern at lines 201, 298 and 922
Socket.IO allows any origin (cors_allowed_origins='*')
Flask SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded string when OAuth is off
CORS origins default to http://localhost:3000
FRONTEND_URL defaults to http://localhost:3000 for the email verification link
FRONTEND_URL defaults to http://localhost:3000 for OAuth login and consent redirects
Email link base comes from the request front_url and falls back to http://localhost:3000
Unhandled exceptions return str(error) to the client
POST /auth/verifyEmail has no login or rate limit and sends a verification email to any address
POST /auth/forgotPassword lets anyone trigger a reset for any email, and it also revokes all of that user's OAuth tokens

Login with role 6 (hub) falls back to PartnerProfile when no hub has that email. The hub_id check runs only for role 3 and the path check only when path is sent, so any partner who omits path gets a hub-role token at lines 317-319. edit_mentor lets the hub role edit any mentor, mentee or partner profile, including the login email
Admin CSV and XLSX exports write user-entered fields with no formula escaping

User message text and recent chat history are pasted straight into the moderation prompt with no delimiter or injection guard. A sender can write instructions that tell the classifier not to flag the message.
Moderation fails open. Any OpenAI error (missing key, no credits, oversized text) lets the message through unflagged. The full message text goes to the model with no length cap.
Every sent message makes two paid OpenAI calls (omni moderation plus gpt-5-nano). No per-user rate limit or daily cap exists.

A hardcoded user (one staff email address and its plus aliases) skips message moderation completely. The exemption lives in code, not in a role or config. sender_id comes from the client in several send paths, so a sender can claim that profile id.
Prompt says to flag only when the exact violating words can be quoted. Code checks only that evidence is non-empty and never checks that the quote appears in the message.
Event email links default to http://localhost:3000 when FRONTEND_URL is unset. message_flagging defaults the same variable to the production URL, so one setting has two different defaults.
Admin review email link defaults to http://localhost:3000 when FRONTEND_URL is unset
OIDC issuer defaults to http://localhost:8000 if OAUTH_ISSUER is unset, so id tokens would carry a localhost issuer

Staff roles are defined twice with different values. require_auth treats Admin and Support as staff. The event workflow treats only Admin as staff, so Support passes admin_only routes but cannot review events.
Dev and prod partner ids for a special partner (N50) are hardcoded, and both are checked in every environment
Translation price per page 0.08 is hardcoded in code and is unused
Cloud Storage bucket name hardcoded instead of read from config
Firebase authDomain and storageBucket project ids hardcoded, so dev and prod share one project name
Production site URL hardcoded in security notification emails (also at lines 167 and 208), so dev emails link to prod
Weekly cron calls a hardcoded production URL. The target endpoint has its auth decorator commented out.
A real person's personal email address is the hardcoded default recipient (also in the usage text at line 4)
TODO plus commented-out code that writes to a developer's local home directory path. The translated-document flow is marked unresolved.

Default meeting token is valid for every room (room *) and enables recording, live streaming, outbound calls and transcription. The meeting view issues it with a placeholder name and email to any caller.
Meeting feature flags (livestreaming, recording, outbound-call, transcription, moderator) hardcoded to true in code

Bug report attachments take a client-chosen content type with no type allowlist and no per-file size check. They upload to the public images bucket and return a public URL from a no-login endpoint, so HTML or malware can be hosted on the org bucket.

Paid Google Translate is called once per target language for each text field with no rate limit or length cap. It is reachable from training library routes that have no login check. Event drafts by any mentor or mentee also trigger it (event_workflow.py 468).
A bare except keeps the untranslated original as the translation for any language that fails. Records save as translated with English or source-file content.

Admin alert emails are rate limited per exception type and endpoint. For frontend reports, the endpoint comes from the request body and the IP limit trusts X-Forwarded-For, so an anonymous caller can trigger unlimited alert emails.
The sensitive-key filter misses names like pass and client_secret, so those values can be stored in ErrorLog request payloads
VerifiedEmail stores an admin-supplied password in plain text and prints it in __repr__. Users.py lines 19-20 also keep legacy plain password and pin fields.
A new mentee profile without an email gets the placeholder email@gmail.com saved as a real address (TODO admits it)
Partner profile edit accepts restricted, assign_mentors and assign_mentees from the request body. A partner can change admin-controlled assignment and restriction fields.
A mentee (and a mentor at lines 334-359) can set organization to any partner id and is auto-added to that partner's assigned list. That grants partner-scoped events and content with no approval.
Dockerfile says it is used for production but runs manage.py runserver, which starts socketio with debug=True on 0.0.0.0
The file has only negation rules, so nothing is excluded. COPY . /app ships any local .env, firebase_service_key.json, keys/oidc-private.pem and creds.ini into the image.
Full response body of every 4xx and 5xx is logged at debug level, and the app also writes debug logs to app.log
get_allowed_scope grants any requested scope when allowed_scopes is empty. The authorize view rejects unknown scopes, so the impact is limited to token-endpoint paths.
send_sms (Twilio) and send_email have no rate limit. The unread_alert route that calls them has its auth decorator commented out, so anyone can trigger paid SMS and email to any user id repeatedly.
Firebase web config in client code. apiKey comes from REACT_APP_FIREBASE_API_KEY and the project id, app id and measurement id are hardcoded. Public by design
API and front-end base URLs hardcoded per build: mentee-dev.herokuapp.com, app.menteeglobal.org, localhost:8000 and localhost:3000
N50 partner id hardcoded as two Mongo ObjectIds (dev and prod). The backend keeps its own copy as N50_ID_DEV and N50_ID_PROD
Bot API origin hardcoded: localhost:8001 locally and the production bot everywhere else, so the dev Heroku tier also logs into the production bot. Line 78 repeats the prod URL

Admin and private pages are gated by the role stored in localStorage (getRole). PrivateRoute and App.js work the same way. Setting role=0 in devtools opens the admin screens, though the data APIs still check the token

Support 'log in as this user' only rewrites localStorage role, profileId and support_user_id. Same in MenteeCard, PartnerCard, HubCard and useAuth.js. There is no server-side impersonation session or audit. It relies on the backend letting the SUPPORT role pass every role check

The client listens to every socket event and keeps only events named after its own profileId. Filtering happens in the browser because the server broadcasts each direct message to all connected sockets
Direct message body goes into dangerouslySetInnerHTML after a regex linkify, with no escaping. The backend stores the raw body, so this is stored XSS

Group message body goes into dangerouslySetInnerHTML through formatMessageText, which adds mention spans and links but never escapes the HTML. This is stored XSS. Participant names also go unescaped into new RegExp
The rule 'application approved and training done' is checked only in the browser before profile creation. POST /api/account has no login and never checks the application state

The training-complete gate is only a disabled button (allChecked). The page identity is just ?email= and ?role= in the URL (lines 18-21). The backend route that advances the application has no login and does not check training status

Hiding private mentee profiles and restricted-partner scoping are decided by query params the browser sets (all, show_private, exclude_restricted, restricted_partner_id). The search route has no login and obeys them
Mentor gallery restrictions (paused mentors, restricted partner scope) are set by client params all, show_paused and exclude_restricted. The backend search has no login and trusts them
After booking, the mentee's browser rewrites the mentor's whole availability list through PUT /availability/<mentorId>. Removing the booked slot should happen on the server
The 18+ age rule for mentees is checked only in the browser. The backend mentee form takes age as a free string with no minimum
getIsEmailVerified sends email and password in a GET query string, so they show up in server and proxy logs. The target route is admin-only, so this verify flow also fails for normal users

The client sends front_url (FRONT_BASE_URL or window.location.href) and the backend builds links in outgoing emails from it. Same pattern at api.js 360, 565, 603, 679, 887, 1232 and 2301. A caller can put a phishing link into official emails
Bulk add users fires the upload without awaiting it or checking the result, then always shows 'Successfully added users!'
Download helpers swallow errors (catch console.error, and downloadBlob returns silently), so 'Downloaded ... successfully' shows even when the export failed
Partner export helpers swallow errors and resolve, so 'Mentees Excel downloaded!' shows on failure. Same at 964-973, 1005-1014 and 1035-1044
updateBugReport and deleteBugReportById catch errors and resolve, so the try never fails and the 'updated' or 'deleted successfully' toast always shows
The signed PDF is built in the browser and shown as signed. saveSignedDoc is fired without await or a result check, so the user sees a signed agreement even if the upload failed
The copy-link success toast shows before the clipboard write, which runs later in a setTimeout. If that write fails, success was already shown. Same at lines 73-92
Editing a group message updates the UI locally and emits the socket event without an ack, so the edit looks saved even if the server rejects it
Five placeholder trainings ('Mentee Handbook', a lorem ipsum id, an ant.design URL) become the list data whenever trainingData is undefined. A skeleton covers them only while loading
Hardcoded sample message from a fake sender as the default drawer item. The component is unused because its usage in Navigation.js line 31 is commented out
The view or book permission gate is only client state (verified). The password state is never set, so the check always sends undefined
Attention-rule labels hardcode a 14-day threshold in UI text, separate from the backend logic that applies it
